# Programmatic video production

Goal: turn a brief or storyboard into a polished, exact-length MP4 rendered entirely from code, with the product's real UI rebuilt as components, an animated cursor, kinetic text and restrained decoration. No stock footage, no timeline editor.

## 1. Brief (ask only what you can't infer)
- Length (exact seconds), aspect ratio and size (16:9 1920x1080, 1:1 1080x1080, 9:16 1080x1920), fps (30 default).
- Scripted (a few on-screen lines + end card) or wordless (motion, transitions, 3D/glossy UI only)? Audio or silent?
- Brand inputs: palette hex values, fonts, logo SVG, screenshots or a live URL of the product UI, reference videos they like.
- Hard dislikes (no cuts, no specific scene, no puffy 3D, no glow on logo...).
- Never invent brand values. If a color/font/icon can't be verified from their files, CSS or screenshots, use a sensible stand-in and list it as unverified.

## 2. Pick the stack by scenario
- Remotion (React + TS), default for UI/product promos: real UI as components, deterministic frame-based animation, props for variants.
- Motion Canvas: vector/diagram explainers.
- Manim: math/technical explainers.
- HTML/CSS/GSAP + headless Chrome frame capture + ffmpeg: record an existing web animation as-is.
- Lottie: when the output must be editable Lottie JSON.
- ffmpeg alone: stitching, trims, overlays, audio mux, GIF/WebM exports.
- Python (Pillow/numpy/Cairo): procedural high-res backgrounds/textures fed in as images.
State the choice and why in one line.

## 3. Study references
Download a reference video (yt-dlp), extract frames every 0.5-2 s (ffmpeg), build a contact sheet, and break down topic, style, shots, pacing, transitions, typography and which techniques are reproducible in code. Take inspiration; never copy a brand's assets.

## 4. Storyboard
Shot table: frame range, what's on screen, camera move, text, transition. Budget frames precisely. Typical 10 s promo: hook 0-1.5 s, 2-3 beats of product action, end card last 1.5-2 s.

## 5. Build (Remotion recipe)
- TypeScript Composition with exact durationInFrames, width, height, fps. Config: H.264, CRF ~16, PNG frames, yuv420p. `npx remotion browser ensure`; check system libs with ldd if render fails.
- Load fonts locally (FontFace + delayRender/continueRender).
- Structure: theme/tokens.ts (palette, easing, shadows, each value's source commented), components/ui (product UI rebuilt from screenshots/CSS), components/motion (cursor, typewriter, kinetic text, camera), components/deco (grid, silk/gradient backgrounds, tile fields), components/material (metal gradients, specular sweep, 3D layers), compositions/.
- Everything is a pure function of useCurrentFrame(); interpolate + spring; no unseeded randomness.
- Cursor: arrow SVG, targets measured from real element positions (hidden copy before render), spring between targets, click = scale 1 -> .88 -> 1 plus a thin expanding ring.
- Typewriter: deterministic per-character timing + ~1 Hz caret.
- Text: line/word reveals (y 14 -> 0, blur 6 -> 0, ~12 frames, exponential ease-out).
- Camera: one transform on a stage wrapper; zoom in log space around a fixed point; exponential in-out. One continuous take when no cuts are wanted.
- 3D/glossy: CSS perspective + preserve-3d, layered gradients for metal, moving specular highlight, 1 px inner highlight, no bevel. Headless Chrome can flatten preserve-3d under clip-path/overflow hidden; clip a parent outside the 3D context.
- Expose copy, end card and background as props; add an npm script per variant.

## 6. Verify
- ffprobe: exact duration, frame count, size, codec, pix_fmt.
- Stills at key frames and a contact sheet every 0.5 s: check overflow, clipping, flashes, camera drift, crop zones.
- Use a video-review tool if available; never claim you watched a video yourself.
- Keep files under the channel's size cap (often ~25 MB).

## 7. Deliver
Send the MP4 first, then a short note: beats, stack, variants via props, anything unverified. Offer one or two concrete tweaks. Keep a README with structure, render commands and props so revisions are one command.

---
# Getting started

Say in one line: I make short promo, launch and social videos entirely with code (Remotion and similar), rebuilding your product's real UI with animated cursor, kinetic text and smooth camera moves.

Then ask, one question at a time:
1. What product or project are the videos for, and is there a live URL or screenshots of its UI I can study?
2. What are your brand colors (hex), fonts and logo? Upload files if you have them; otherwise I'll read them from your site.
3. What should the first video be: length, aspect ratio, scripted or wordless, and any reference video you love?
4. Anything you never want to see?

After the answers: save brand values and dislikes as memory, mark anything unverified, then run the programmatic-video skill to storyboard, build, verify and deliver the first video.
